chapter: Booker T. Washington Community Center Band
title: Alto and mellophone, and moving up chair by chair
summary: Both were E-flat instruments playing the same parts; players moved up as others shifted to trombones or trumpets, and the kids helped one another.

bands.name: Booker T. Washington Community Center Band

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up the horn: first instrument and the trombone

blocks.x: Yeah. Moreso than the alto horn, huh?
Yeah, well, both of them served about the same purpose.
There wasn't much difference in them.

Pitched to E-Flat, you know. And you played the same music. If the music says E-Flat Alto, you play the mellophone. Yeah, first, second and third. See, in the first place you've got to move up. See, when they put you in there, I started down as third -- I mean fourth alto.
And then you move up to -- maybe another one of the guys goes in the trombone section, see.
Which in our case it did happen. The first man went in the trombone section, and then I'd move up to third, and some other guy would come in and play fourth, you know.
Then finally another one would move up to -- maybe he'd go over in the trumpet section and then I'd move up to second.
Then pretty soon some other guy would go over -- maybe like when Dunc left, I think Duncan's brother started to play the baritone.
When he left, then -- in fact he died, you know, and then one of the alto players went over there, so then -- the first alto went over there, and I moved up to first.
Then later -- you were always moving, you know.

I enjoyed it. I really enjoyed it. And with all the kids, if there was something you didn't understand, why they would -- you'd say, 'How does this go here,' you know, and they would show you how it would go.
Yeah, so you didn't have to worry or --
